description: We are a team of students passionate about space exploration, science, and innovation. Through the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to combine creativity, technology, and storytelling to bring space exploration to life, inspire curiosity, and share the incredible discoveries that have shaped our understanding of the universe.
summary: Echoes Beyond Earth is an immersive, interactive storytelling website that brings the forgotten stories of space exploration back to life. Inspired by NASA's Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge, our project explores the spacecraft, landers, and rovers left behind after completing their missions, reminding us that even when their signals fall silent, their contributions to humanity continue. Our goal is to encourage curiosity, deepen appreciation for the technology and people behind space exploration, and show that a mission's end does not mean the end of its story, because even when the machines fall silent, their stories still echo beyond Earth.
details:
Echoes Beyond Earth is an interactive storytelling website that brings the stories of retired spacecraft and equipment left behind in space to life. Visitors can explore Mars, the Moon, and Beyond through animated journeys, real NASA images, and first-person stories told from the spacecraft's perspective. Our goal is to make space exploration history more engaging, memorable, and accessible, especially for younger audiences. Instead of simply presenting facts, we combine science, creativity, and emotion to help visitors understand each mission's discoveries and lasting impact.

We developed our website using React, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS, with Figma for design, VS Code for development, GitHub for collaboration, and Netlify for publishing. We also used NASA's mission records and imagery to keep our stories scientifically accurate, alongside AI-assisted tools for coding and design.

As a two-person team, we focused on creating smooth animations, interactive features, and unique storytelling experiences for different missions. Ultimately, we want to show that even when a spacecraft's mission ends, its discoveries and legacy continue to inspire future exploration.
